main_body: Gabled house: a large terracotta tile roof (rows 2-42) over a cream plaster and timber-frame front wall (rows 44-78) with an arched door and a shuttered window
top_band: Terracotta roof slope, light salmon at the top (row ~4) darkening to deep red-brown at the eave (row ~42). It runs from row 2 to row 42 and reads as a slope seen from above
evidence: Down the middle column, the tiled roof slope has a clear tone gradient and per-tile courses. It ends in a dark eave line at rows ~40-42, and the plaster wall sits below it with its own timber frame. The roof is a real sloped top surface, as in the Beodeul house references, so it is not a thin cap. The door has a stone surround and a dark arch inset. The window has shutters, a sill and a dark top edge, so the front is inset rather than flat. There is no receding side face.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tone steps, with tile courses, per-tile highlights and dark red-brown joints. The outlines are tinted dark brown and red-brown, not black. The plaster wall has speckle, and the stone base and door planks are shaded. It is slightly plainer than the references, which have half-timber diagonals, chimney detail and stone texture. The wall areas are fairly open, but they carry speckle and so are not flat fills. It would sit acceptably next to the reference.
